claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Are you (or your partner, if you have one) responsible for Alex? This means you're taking care of Alex's day-to-day needs, such as providing food, clothing, and a place to live.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I take care of all their day-to-day needs - food, clothing, everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** 

(Full-time non-advanced education typically means school, sixth form, or college courses up to A-level standard or equivalent, and usually involves at least 12 hours per week of supervised study.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - they're studying for their A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I need to ask about your immigration and residence status:

**Are you (the person claiming) living in the UK, and do you have the right to reside here?** For example, are you a UK citizen, have settled status, or have another immigration status that allows you to live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I'm a UK citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex also living in the UK with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives here with me in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed priority over you for Child Benefit (for example, if Alex spends time living with another person)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me taking care of them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old
- Alex lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex's day-to-day needs (food, clothing, accommodation)
- Alex is in full-time approved education (studying for A-levels)
- You are a UK citizen living in the UK
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the UK Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 16, in full-time approved education (A-levels), lives with you, and you're responsible for them, you meet all the eligibility criteria.

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- You're a UK citizen living in the UK
- You're responsible for Alex who lives with you
- Alex is 16 and in approved education (A-levels)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex as long as they continue in approved education or training and remain under 20 years old.

**Important note:** If you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.
